 In Re : CRAN 1 of 2025:
 1.
The petitioner/appellant is the sole convict.
His parents have been acquitted in the trial held in connection with the charges under Sections 498A/304B of the Indian Penal Code.
The petitioner is the husband of the deceased lady.
2. Learned Advocate for the petitioner says that there are sufficient loopholes in the prosecution case.
The petitioner has been sentenced to suffer imprisonment for eight years.
It is a term imprisonment.
Generally in case of term imprisonment, the appeal court should grant bail as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kiran Kumar-Vs.-State of M.P., reported in (2001) 9 SCC 211.

sentences.text: 3. Learned State Counsel strongly opposes the bail prayer.
He draws our attention to the depositions of PWs 1, 2 and 3.
He says that there is sufficient incriminating evidence showing the guilt of the petitioner.
4. We have considered the facts and circumstances of the case and the material on record.
On a prima facie assimilation of the evidence on record, it appears that there are contradictions in the evidence of various witnesses recorded by the learned Trial Court.

Further, it is a sentence of term imprisonment of eight years out of which about one year one month has already been served by the petitioner taking into account the pre-conviction period of detention.
There is also no possibility of an early hearing of the appeal.
5. From a departmental note dated November 20, 2025, we see that defects have been noted by the Record Examiner.
Therefore, there is no chance of an early hearing of the appeal.

6. In view of the aforesaid, we are inclined to allow this application for suspension of sentence.
7.

Accordingly the appellant, namely, Munshi Sahnawaz @ Munshi Sahanawaz @ Sahanawaj Munshi @ Dulal, shall be released on bail upon furnishing bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand), with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Alipore and on further condition that the appellant shall not leave the geographical limits of district South 24 Parganas and on further conditions that the appellant shall meet the Inspector-in- Charge of the Polerhat police station once a fortnight and further that the appellant shall be personally present or be represented before this Court when the appeal is taken up for hearing.
8.

10. We clarify that the observations made by us in this order are only for the purpose of disposing of the application for suspension of sentence and the same shall have no relevance at the final hearing of the appeal.
